source: Build the service with Java 25 and Spring Boot 4.0.1. Add dependency org.example:widget:2.3.0, set widget.timeout=750ms, then run ./mvnw test. Start the app and verify GET /widgets/42 returns HTTP 200 with status=ready. If port 8080 is occupied, set server.port=0 before retrying.

Atlas (https://example.com/atlas) targets Java 25 scaffolding and starts with atlas init. Beacon (https://example.com/beacon) supports Java 21 and focuses on testing with beacon verify. Choose Atlas for new Spring Boot 4 projects; choose Beacon when retrofitting tests into an existing Java 21 service. Atlas does not support legacy Boot 2 applications.

A cache stampede occurs when many clients recompute the same expired value simultaneously. The causal chain is synchronized expiry, concurrent misses, duplicate backend work, and overload. A per-key single-flight guard interrupts that chain. It is unnecessary when values expire at staggered times and recomputation is already cheap. Apply the idea by measuring duplicate work before adding coordination.

source: On 2026-06-30, a single-region experiment measured 240 requests. The new path had p95 latency of 180ms with a 95% confidence interval of 160-205ms, versus 225ms for the control. Requests were sampled only during daytime traffic, so the result does not establish multi-region or overnight performance. The evidence supports a larger rollout experiment, not an immediate global launch.
